svg.title: Every pure input with any inert reference therefore gives pure outputs of overlap √pm, whose half trace distance is √1 −pm. Convexity handles mixed inputs. This proves the upper bound uniformly over references. For any competing bath of dimension at most b, apply its isometry and the target isometry to a maximally entangled input. The competitor output has Schmidt rank at most b across bath versus pointer–memory–reference. After any bath-only identification it lies in some bath subspace of dimension at most b. Its squared overlap with the target is at most the target mass in that subspace, at most the largest-b eigenvalue sum of its bath marginal. The target pure state’s nonzero bath eigenvalues are those of ρA, so this sum is pm for b = 3m. Pure-state trace distance is thus at least √1 −pm. This proves (35). □
